blocking.section: Threat model and trust boundaries (Figure 1, OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14 answer); Transport security (hop table)
blocking.issue: The Scope promises "transport and identity for every hop", but the hops that carry secrets are missing from Figure 1, the threat table and the hop table. These are Node to Vault for `vault` secretRef, Node to the Kubernetes API for `kubernetes` secretRef and `kubernetes` discovery, and Ruralz Control to the Kubernetes API for the CRD watch. The hop table gives no TLS or peer-authentication rule for Vault or the Kubernetes API, although a security engineer needs exactly that to approve a `vault` or `kubernetes` provider. The answer to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14 is also incomplete compared with its source. Control plane and GitOps lists token replica join (TB-11) and a Kubernetes client (service account) as new crossings, but this document maps only to TB-5, TB-7, TB-8 and TB-13. Figure 1 still has no Ruralz Control to OCI registry TB-8 edge, although the answer adopts that crossing.
blocking.evidence: Line 24: "In scope: ... transport and identity for every hop". Line 109: "For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14, option (a), its new crossings map to TB-5, TB-7, TB-8 and TB-13." Line 338: "`kubernetes` (`get` and `watch` in the Node's namespace only) and `vault` (Node authentication: OQ-security-and-identity-10) are Planned (M2)". This is the only mention, with no hop row. Control plane and GitOps line 589: "This design adds crossings ... token `Enroll` (TB-5), token replica join (TB-11), HMAC webhooks, Ruralz Control as OCI registry client ... and Kubernetes client (service account), and the relay on 8092 (TB-13)." Figure 1 has `gw -->|"TB-8 ..."| oci` but no `ctl --> oci` edge and no Vault or Kubernetes API node.
blocking.fix: (1) Add a 'Secret providers and Kubernetes API' node to Figure 1, with gw and ctl edges labeled with an existing TB ID (for example TB-3 for Node secret and discovery fetches, TB-7 or TB-11 for Ruralz Control's Kubernetes client), or propose new IDs in OQ-security-and-identity-29 for System overview. Also add a `ctl -->|"TB-8"| oci` edge. (2) Add a hop-table row: "Vault, Kubernetes API (TB-x) | TLS 1.2 or newer, server verified, never cleartext | Vault auth per OQ-security-and-identity-10; namespace-scoped service account | Planned (M2)". (3) Add a threat row for compromise or spoofing of the secret provider, with its mitigation. (4) Extend the OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14 sentence to name TB-11 for token replica join and the boundary chosen for the Kubernetes client.

blocking.section: Authorization (IP filtering and GeoIP); Open questions (OQ-security-and-identity-6)
blocking.issue: Foundation pack section 10 assigns the derivation of the client address behind trusted proxies to this document. The document does not derive it. It sends the whole question to OQ-security-and-identity-6, owned by configuration-model, lists three options with none proposed, and only warns operators away from IP-based controls. Running behind a load balancer is the most common production topology. There, `authz.ip`, `source.ip` Rate Limit keys and the throttle's source key are all unusable, and so is the Configuration model's own `overridable: false` `ratelimit-global` keyed on `source.ip`. OQ-observability-4 (b), which this document recommends, also depends on trusted proxies. Operators cannot act, and nobody else owns the rule, since no other document mentions trusted proxies or X-Forwarded-For.
blocking.evidence: Pack line 379: "`authz.ip` allows or denies by CIDR on the client address; deriving that address behind trusted proxies belongs to Security and identity." Line 305: "Until trusted proxies exist (OQ-security-and-identity-6), deployments behind a load balancer SHOULD NOT rely on `authz.ip`, `source.ip` Rate Limit keys or the throttle's source key, which collapse to one key." Line 533: "| OQ-security-and-identity-6 | How are trusted proxies declared? | (a) CIDR list; (b) PROXY protocol v2; (c) Both | configuration-model | Yes, for `source.ip` users |"
blocking.fix: Add a short 'Client address' rule under IP filtering. For example: "`source.ip` is the TCP or QUIC peer, unless the peer is in the trusted-proxy CIDR list. Then it is the rightmost `X-Forwarded-For` (or `Forwarded`) address not in the list, or the PROXY protocol v2 source on listeners that opt in. Headers from untrusted peers are overwritten, never appended." Mark the rule Planned (M1) and tag any limits (target). Change OQ-security-and-identity-6 to recommend option (c), marked (proposed), for the fields. Make security-and-identity co-owner for the semantics, since the pack assigns them here, with configuration-model owning the fields.

blocking.issue: The document claims a property the design does not have. T1 and the throttle table say the throttle 'never locks out'. But the username bucket (burst 10, refill 1 per second) is shared by the attacker and the real owner. A flood of wrong passwords for one username keeps that bucket empty, so the owner's verifications that miss the success cache wait 2 s and get 429 RZ-AUTH-007 for as long as the flood lasts. That is a targeted lockout, and the residual-trade-off sentence effectively admits it. The document also leaves two things undefined that an operator needs to judge the risk. It does not say whether a success-cache hit refreshes the 60 s entry, which decides whether a steady legitimate client is ever re-throttled. It does not say whether an unknown username computes a hash. Without that rule, an attacker who sprays many usernames gets a fresh burst of 10 for each and can fill the Node-wide hash queue (GOMAXPROCS slots, 4 x GOMAXPROCS waiters). Every `auth.basic` caller outside the success cache then gets 429.
blocking.evidence: Line 86: "| T1 | Credential guessing, hash-cost exhaustion, targeted lockout | TB-1 | 128-bit keys; [throttle](#pre-authentication-throttling) that delays, never locks out |". Line 400: "| Username bucket | Burst 10, refill 1 per second, in a 64-shard LRU of 100,000 usernames (target); an empty bucket delays up to 2 s (target), then RZ-AUTH-007, and never locks out |". Line 402: "| Hash queue | `GOMAXPROCS` slots, 4 x `GOMAXPROCS` waiters, 1 s deadline (target); overflow gets RZ-AUTH-007 unhashed |". Line 404: "Residual trade-off (T1, OQ-security-and-identity-15): under a flood against one username, its owner shares the bucket's rate."
blocking.fix: (1) Replace 'never locks out' with an accurate statement, for example "no permanent lockout; under a sustained flood against one username, that user is throttled while the flood lasts (residual, OQ-security-and-identity-15)". Or change the design so the owner is protected, for example by giving a separate small bucket to sources that authenticated that username successfully in the last 24 h (target). (2) State that a success-cache hit refreshes the entry, or that it does not. (3) State how unknown usernames are handled, for example "an unknown username computes one dummy hash under the same bucket and queue". Add a sentence and a T1 note that spraying across usernames is bounded only by the Node-wide hash queue, with the metric that exposes it. (4) Add both residuals to OQ-security-and-identity-15.

blocking.section: Open questions (inherited list); Control plane security (Signed Revisions and Plugin artifacts)
blocking.issue: This document owns OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24, but neither the inherited list nor any section addresses it. The question is about ADR-0017, which this document also owns: whether key rotation re-signs retained Revisions, and whether a Last-Known-Good verified before an emergency key removal still boots. The Signed Revisions section says nothing about emergency removal. A security engineer therefore cannot tell from the owning document whether, after an emergency removal of the online key, a Node still boots a Last-Known-Good signed by that key. Control plane and GitOps already says it does.
blocking.evidence: Control plane and GitOps line 617: "| OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24 | Should ADR-0017 and Security and identity adopt rotation re-signing and booting a Last-Known-Good verified before an emergency removal? | (a) Adopt (proposed); (b) such Nodes boot not ready | security-and-identity | No |". Line 246 there: "a Last-Known-Good verified before an emergency removal still boots (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24)". Line 558 here lists the answered and deferred inherited questions without OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24. The only rotation text here is line 134: "signing keys arrive in a root-signed `TrustUpdate` before use".
blocking.fix: Add one sentence to Signed Revisions and Plugin artifacts that decides it. For example: "For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24, option (a): rotation re-signs retained Revisions, assignments and promotions; a Last-Known-Good verified before an emergency removal still boots, and it is reported as a degraded state until a Revision signed by a current key arrives." Alternatively choose (b) and state the consequence that such Nodes boot not ready. Add the ID to the 'Answered above' list.

blocking.issue: The engine-memory bound contradicts System overview. System overview gives peak configuration memory as (K + 2) times the snapshot size, with K = 2 retired snapshots: the active snapshot, two retired ones and the candidate being compiled. This document says engine memory stays under three times the Revision-wide ceiling, which leaves out the candidate being compiled. When engine data changes between Revisions, the shared-by-digest reuse does not help, and the peak is four times the ceiling. Operators sizing Nodes from this document would under-provision by about 64 MiB (target).
blocking.evidence: Line 291: "A Revision-wide ceiling of 64 MiB of engine data and 50,000 entities (target) ... counts against the Node compile budget ([System overview](01-system-overview.md#compile-before-swap)), so with two retired snapshots engine memory stays under three times it (target)." System overview line 342: "Peak configuration memory is (K + 2) times snapshot size (hypothesis)", with "At most K = 2 retired snapshots are kept (target)".
blocking.fix: Change the sentence to "so at peak, during a compile with two retired snapshots, engine memory stays under (K + 2) = four times it (target), less where unchanged engines are shared by content digest". Keep the System overview anchor.

non_blocking.suggestion: Keys "outlive failed refreshes by 1 hour as a degraded state", which uses keys past their `max-age`. System overview TB-10 says "Cached keys until expiry, then fail closed". Define expiry as `max-age` plus the 1-hour stale grace (target), or add TB-10 to OQ-security-and-identity-29, so readers of both documents do not see a contradiction.

For OQ-ai-llm-gateway-12 (b), `auth.upstream-sigv4` is Upstream-scoped, but one `ai` Upstream can reach candidates of several dialects, for example Bedrock falling back to Anthropic. This also keeps the design consistent with the AI/LLM gateway rule that Upstream-scoped Policies on an `ai` Upstream do not set credential headers.
